text.p: Italian debt markets came to rest in negative territory at the end of a quiet session, moving contrary to the general direction of other bond markets.

Traders said futures, which had held their ground earlier in the day, were worn down by sales from the U.S. The March Btp future on LIFFE was 30 basis points off and testing support at 131.00. Another prop lay in the 130.70/80 region, dealers said.

The November 2006 Btp ended 23 basis points in the red at 104.68, yielding 7.19 percent with a spread of 158 basis points over the 10-year Bund. The most traded July 2006 Btp was 24 basis points weaker at 110.70.
The market remained technically relatively positive.

Dealers said fundamentally it was helped by comments from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer at the weekend that Italy would be assessed like everyone else when judgement day came for taking part in a single European currency.

This helped to assuage concerns, fuelled by a newpaper report last week, that there were plans afoot to get Italy to delay EMU entry, all vehemently denied by Brussels, Bonn and Rome. "It alleviated pressure on Italy," one dealer commented.
